boundary_rationale: Onset: Ezek.44.1 opens with a returning-transport verb that reopens the vision frame after the utterance close and double samekh at Ezek.43.27. The prophet is shown the shut east gate and told its meaning (44.2), with the prince's privilege attached (44.3); 44.4 carries a further transport verb (a fresh entry by the north gate) and closes with the prostration formula 'I fell on my face,' matching the vision's own inclusio elsewhere (1.28, 3.23, 11.13, 43.3). Close: the prostration at 44.4 is weighed against the immediately following verse, Ezek.44.5, which opens with a fresh son-of-man address and a directive to mark, see and hear the house's ordinances -- a class shift from vision narrative to statute. Both sides of the seam are text-signalled: the vision's own close-device on one side, a fresh address opening a distinct instructional mode on the other.

boundary_rationale: Onset weighed both sides: Ezek.45.18 carries BOTH a full month+day date formula AND the messenger formula in the same verse -- the exact combination that reads like a fresh oracle onset. On the onset side, the messenger formula (also present at 44.6, 44.9, 45.9, 46.1, 46.16, 47.13) opens what looks like a new speech; but the date clause carries no year word, so it fails the book's structural dateline test (a YEAR word together with a month or day term) -- it is one of exactly four calendar dates in the book (45.18, 45.20, 45.21, 45.25) that carry a month/day construction without a year, and none of the book's fourteen year-bearing datelines falls anywhere across 44.1-48.35. On the close side, the law paragraph before it (45.9-17) already closed at the Ezek.45.17 samekh, and the addressee and topic (the cultic calendar under the temple-law section opened at 45.9) do not change at 45.18 -- there is no addressee-class shift of the kind that would corroborate a fresh onset. Reading 45.18 as an onset would put a false boundary inside the single festival-calendar paragraph that runs 45.18-25 as one unit: New Year sanctuary cleansing (18-20, itself containing the non-dateline calendar date at 45.20), Passover (21-24, containing the non-dateline calendar date at 45.21), and the seventh-month feast (25, containing the non-dateline calendar date at 45.25). Close: the samekh recorded after Ezek.45.25 closes both the calendar-law paragraph and the chapter.

boundary_rationale: Onset: the messenger formula at Ezek.46.1 opens the Sabbath/new-moon gate rule, itself carrying the construction glossed 'the (day of the) new moon' -- disclosed as a chodesh-root homograph, not a date formula (recurring at 46.6); the construction glossed 'at the new moons' recurs at 46.3, the same homograph family as Ezek.45.17. The unit runs through the prince's Sabbath offering (4-8), the people's festival entry-and-exit rule (9-10), the feast-day meal offering (11-12), and the daily burnt offering (13-15), where Ezek.46.13's 'a lamb of its first year' carries a year word that is explicitly NOT a dateline.
